image_description: A close-up studio shot of a black compression driver (horn tweeter) against a white background. The device features a large, flared exponential horn mouth, a central phase plug assembly, and a mounting flange at the base with screw holes. A red label with white text is visible on the cylindrical throat section.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: There are no visible diaphragm cones (woofers/tweeters with flexible surrounds). Instead, there is a rigid horn structure and a phase plug. This is a distinct type of transducer housing.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Prominent large woofer dominating the front face with a much smaller tweeter positioned above or beside it.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible surfaces are hard plastic or metal (horn and casing), not the flexible cone materials described.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Grille cloth or perforated metal may cover the drivers.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Terminal connections visible on rear panel.

The object is clearly identifiable as an audio transducer component.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The text on the red label is illegible and distorted. Characters appear to melt into each other ('...V...'), lacking the sharp edges expected of printed industrial labels. This is a common AI artifact.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The interior of the horn lacks the expected smooth, matte, or slightly textured finish of molded plastic/metal. It appears overly smooth and digitally airbrushed, with unnatural lighting gradients that don't fully match the exterior reflections.
The screw holes in the mounting flange appear slightly irregular in shape (not perfect circles/ovals), suggesting minor geometric distortion typical of generative models.
